summary: Extract files from COCOSID2.DSK, including deleted ones
description: Done before tracking began (commit ddd84e6). tools/decb_extract.py pulls the one live file, files/COCOSID.BIN (7,800 bytes, LOADM, exec $4800). Five deleted directory entries plus one orphan were recovered by hand into files/deleted/ by reading contiguous granules 35-62: each parses as a complete LOADM file, they tile the granules exactly, and lengths match the surviving entries' last-sector byte counts. The deleted files' names were first guessed (SPRITE, GOLF, JOYTEST2) and later settled by #13: all six are byte-identical to the author's CoCo 3 demo disk, so GOLF.BIN was renamed WOLF.BIN, UNNAMED-G35.BIN SCALE.BIN and COCOSID-OLD.BIN COCOSID-COCO3.BIN. Not done: decb_extract.py does not do the deleted-file recovery itself (see #7).

Done before tracking began (commits ddd84e6, d7ef2f6). tools/dis6809.py is a code-tracing 6809 disassembler emitting lwasm source; cocosid.asm reassembles byte for byte (lwasm --format=decb, cmp against files/COCOSID.BIN). Needed: DP=$48 globally, DP=$49 for the self-modifying sample loop $494C-$4983, and the nine BRA entries of the command table at $49F7 (reached via JMP [$4806]). Verified mechanically by the round trip, not by the user.

Done before tracking began (commit d7ef2f6). Labels, symbols, comments and trace options live in cocosid.ann and are merged by dis6809.py -a, so cocosid.asm stays generated. Documents the voice record (V_* fields), MIXER and the self-modifying SAMPLOOP, the sequencer and command table, PWM sweep and wave table construction. Timing figures (77 cycles/sample, 227 samples/pass) are from cycle counting; see #5 for checking them.

summary: Isolate and document the song data
description: Done before tracking began (commit 8d4778c). tools/songdump.py decodes $542D-$6394 into song/song.asm (NOTE/INSTR/DEFINS/FRAME/BEND/BRATE/ENDPAT macros, note names, tick positions); cocosid.asm INCLUDEs it and still reassembles byte for byte. song/README.md covers format, timing, tuning, instruments and quirks (SONG3 ends inside the pattern table via entry 0 = $2C00). Song length 3,936 ticks from a simulation of the sequencer. Instrument descriptions come from reading frames, not listening (see #6).

summary: Measure tick length and tuning in XRoar
description: song/README.md estimates a tick at about 53,600 cycles (60 ms; 3 x 17,724 for MIXER plus sequencer and PWM), a song length of about 3 min 56 s, and an effective sample rate of about 11.4 kHz, so A4 (note 69) near 425 Hz, roughly half a semitone flat. All of this is from cycle counting. Check it: e.g. run headless (xroar -no-ratelimit with -trap pc=0x48D7 snapshots, or count emulated time between restarts via a trap on RESTART $4871) and correct the README figures. The user has heard it run in XRoar but nobody has timed it. Update from #13: the author's source (Color Computer Archive, 'CocoSiD (Remz) (Coco 2)', cocosid.s) designs for 16.7 notes per second (125 BPM) and gives the song as 123 patterns, 3:56.12, which matches the estimates. That is design intent, not a measurement, so this stays open.

The 'Character' column of the instrument table in song/README.md (bass, snare-type drum, octave-arpeggio pulse, PWM lead, tom drop, ...) was inferred from frame data only. Listen in XRoar (README 'Running it') and correct any that are wrong. A quick way to audition one instrument would be a tiny test song built from song/song.asm.

Recovery of the six files in files/deleted/ was done with an ad-hoc script: for each deleted directory entry (first name byte 0) read contiguous granules from its first granule, parse LOADM blocks to find the true length, and check the last-sector byte count. Fold that into tools/decb_extract.py (e.g. --deleted) so it is reproducible, and also scan free granules with data that no entry claims (granule 35 here).

summary: Compare the CoCo 3 build (COCOSID-COCO3.BIN) with the CoCo 2 build
description: files/deleted/COCOSID-COCO3.BIN (formerly COCOSID-OLD.BIN; 22,833 bytes, exec $4800) is byte-identical to COCOSID.BIN on the author's CoCo 3 disk (Color Computer Archive, 'CocoSiD (Remz) (Coco 3)'). It loads a 14K background picture at $1000. The author's CoCo 3 source is now in third-party/cocosid-coco3/ (cocosid.asm, and the picture cocosid_title_test2.bin), and the CoCo 2 source in third-party/cocosid-coco2/cocosid.s, so a diff of the two original sources is more useful than a fresh disassembly. Record what changed for the CoCo 2 port (GIME setup, picture, VU meter, cycle_ratio 76/92 on pitch bends, sample rate).

summary: Describe the other recovered files (SPRITE, WOLF, JOYTEST2, SCALE)
description: Identified by #13: each is byte-identical to a file on the author's CoCo 3 demo disk, and README.md's recovered-files table now gives the author's own descriptions (from the archived 'Rem's Coco 3 files' page). Remaining: JOYTEST2.BIN (431 bytes) is not described anywhere, and COCOSID2.BIN (3,668 bytes) is small for what the site calls the larger, automatically converted version, so check what it actually is. Low priority: not part of the CoCo 2 player.

summary: Build the player with a different song
description: song/song.asm is now separate source, so a new tune could be assembled into the player. Needs: a check that a changed song still fits before $6395 (WNOISE) or a relocation plan, and a note in song/README.md on writing patterns by hand. Would also allow instrument test songs (#6).

Answered by #13: the author's source header says 'The music "COMMANDO.SID", by Rob Hubbard, has been hand converted to my CoCo synth-player music format', and his site says the same. Recorded in README.md (History) and song/README.md. Closed after user review.

summary: Run COCOSID.BIN in XRoar and document the command
description: Done before tracking began (commit f019b57); user-tested: the user confirmed the tune plays. Command: xroar -machine coco2bus -rompath ~/.xroar/roms -cart rsdos -run files/COCOSID.BIN (README 'Running it'). The first attempt used a nonexistent -rompath (~/roms): XRoar then has no BASIC ROM, the log shows 'Slot 0: (unpopulated)', the screen is garbage and there is no sound. Headless check used -trap pc=0x48D7 / pc=0x4954 snapshots to a .ram file to confirm the sequencer advances.

summary: Research CoCoSID's author and history for the README
description: Found: Color Computer Archive 'Disks/Demos/CocoSiD (Remz) (Coco 2).zip' contains a cocosid.dsk byte-identical to COCOSID2.DSK, plus the original source cocosid.s and listing (13 Feb 2010); source header credits Remi Veilleux, 2010, and Rob Hubbard's Commando. The author's site 'Rem's CoCo 3' (sites.google.com/site/rveilleux, gone; Wayback captures 2012-2016) describes COCOSID, COCOSID2, COCOSID3 and his other CoCo 3 demos. CoCo Central has a post. The six deleted files on our disk match the archive's CoCo 3 disk exactly, so they were renamed. README.md has a sourced History section; song/README.md names the tune. Not used: an AtariAge thread where 'remz' posted a Wolfenstein-style CoCo 3 demo in Dec 2009 (forum blocked automated fetches, so it was not read directly); a games-industry programmer of the same name (no source links the two). The original source is not vendored: the site says 'Copyright (c) 2010 Remi Veilleux' and there is no license. Closed after user review.

summary: Cross-check the disassembly against the original source
description: The author's source for this exact binary is now in third-party/cocosid-coco2/ (cocosid.s and the listing cocosid.lis). Compare it with cocosid.asm / cocosid.ann and song/song.asm: fix any wrong interpretations, and consider adopting the author's names in cocosid.ann (e.g. synth_mixer, selfmod_ldd_freq1, process_voice, rect_modulator, ssynth_* voice fields) or noting them alongside ours.

summary: Add the author's original files in a third-party folder
description: Keep the author's own material found in #13 and later in third-party/, unmodified, with a provenance README (source URL, retrieval date, SHA-256 of each downloaded zip, what was left out and why). Sources: Color Computer Archive 'CocoSiD (Remz) (Coco 2).zip' and '(Coco 3).zip'; Wayback captures of the author's cocosid3.zip and REM_TEXTURE_DEMO.zip. Leave out files that are not his (siddump.exe by Covert Bitops, R-type.sid by Chris Huelsbeck and Ramiro Vaca) and exact duplicates of files already in the repo (the CoCo 2 cocosid.dsk and cocosid.bin). Done: third-party/ holds cocosid-coco2/ (cocosid.s, .lis, .cas), cocosid-coco3/ (demo disk, cocosid.asm, title picture), cocosid3/ (cocosid3.asm, siddump_convert_v3.pl, convert_all.bat) and rem-texture-demo/ (REM_TEXTURE_DEMO.dsk), with provenance and hashes in third-party/README.md and a -text rule in .gitattributes. Closed after user review.

COCOSID2 and COCOSID3 were converted from C64 .sid files (third-party/cocosid3, author's guide). Write docs/sid-format.md describing the PSID/RSID format from the official HVSC specification (cite it), how a .sid player is driven (init/play calls, 50 Hz frames), and how that relates to the author's SIDDUMP -> Perl -> CoCoSID pattern pipeline. Use the R-type.sid header (not in the repo) only as a worked example of field values. Done: docs/sid-format.md summarises the HVSC spec (v1-v5, updated 2026-10-09; linked, not copied): what a .sid is, PSID vs RSID, header fields and flags, R-type.sid as a worked example, and the author's SIDDUMP -> siddump_convert_v3.pl -> .cid pipeline (pulse width is not read by the script). Not covered: the multi-SID v5 details and the full C64 environment setup; the page points to the spec. Closed after user review.
